I AM AN IRONMAN – Ironman Klagenfurt in 10:07:08h!

I’m usually not really the emotional type but here you go:

This was by far the hardest thing I’ve ever done physically (so far 😉).
At the same time, it’s one of the most rewarding, enjoyable, and proudest moments of my life.

I’ve logged over 330 hours of training since January, that’s 14 straight days of training while trying to keep up with work and somewhat of a social life.

During those months, I asked myself more than once:
“Why are you doing this?”
“What are you trying to prove?”
“What’s wrong with you?” 😂

And while I still don’t have the answers to those questions, I do know one thing:
None of this means anything without the people around me.

I may have crossed the finish line alone, but would have never made it there without training partners and friends who pushed and supported me every single day. You guys know who you are, so, Thank you!! 🫶🏼

And to my family. Always there, no matter the distance, no matter the day. I’m endlessly grateful and I wouldn’t be where I am without you! I love you ❤️ 
——————————————————————————————————

And for those asking “What’s next?” - No idea yet… but I’m sure I’ll come up with another stupid idea soon. 😂

Tom, over and out ✌🏼

PS: Race review and more content coming soon…

Ironman Austria 🇦🇹2025 #ironmanaustria2025 

Although it wasn’t the race I wanted! It was one hell of an experience…… one I said many times during the race and after it that “I’m not f**king doing this again” …well, I don’t know about that 😂

The debrief - what I wanted vs what I got

Swim
Wanted 1hr5 or below for this and achieved 1hr8 not a million miles off, but swimming around people and having goggles kicked loose in the first buoy didn’t help. Epic fail also having my tri swim setting as “pool swim” 😭😂
7/10 happy with the result 

T2
Just seemed to be miles away from the swim out (typical Ironman transitions) wanted around 5 mins for this and achieved 5:03 - can’t grumble at that 😂 …. Still only gets 9/10 (always room for improvement) 

Bike 
I was so happy to be out on the bike, I knew @tobybuckley wouldn’t be too far behind but I wasn’t going to risk setting off too quick. Disaster struck 3/4 of the way into the first lap chain issues, then rear derailleur / front mech, despite a race mechanic getting me back moving again, the issue kept arising and I could feel myself burning my matches either struggling through with the wrong gears or trying to make up for lost time with having to physically get off the bike to flick the chain on to the ring I needed. I wanted 5hrs for this and achieved 5hr35 
5/10 happiness score 😡

T2
Wanted 3 mins / achieved 6:06….if I had a swear jar it would have been filled. Flying dismount. Racked the bike and headed to my bag……. Which had co

They screamed: “David…YOU ARE AN IRONMAN!” 🫶
I screamed:“WHERE’S MY SCHNITZEL & BEER?!”🇦🇹 🍺

Finished fried🔥☀️🌡️not broken.✅

3.8 km 🏊🏼180 km 🚴🏼 42 km 🏃

My why is clear — at least most of the time. 😂
Thanks @mrmyuriel and @joelarnosti for helping me live it and showing up when it counted!

IRONMAN

Unbelievable experience to push your body to its limits not just in a single event but every day. The 4am sessions, the long days and sacrifices made, all become worth when you cross that line.

Had a few curve balls with days of rainfall leading up to and still during the race, making for murky waters and slippery bike conditions, along with a loose chain and flat tyre but what better time to dig deep and become your own hero.
With a goal time of sub 12 hours I was a toked to finish in 11:39:14 ⏰

12h05 au Wörthersee 🇦🇹 et presque autant d'heures à gérer ce que je mange.

On me demande souvent ce que j'avale sur un Ironman. Voici tout, chiffres à l'appui : la recharge, le petit-déjeuner à 4h15, le vélo, le marathon… et mon erreur 👉 visuel 8.

La veille, recharge en glucides version locale : des Kärntner Kasnudeln, les raviolis de Carinthie (😋).

Le vélo s'est déroulé comme prévu. Au marathon, je suis parti trop vite, et du 20ème kilomètre au 35ème j'ai payé l'addition. Ce qui m'a permis de finir : marcher à chaque ravitaillement pour boire et manger, puis repartir.

Sur une épreuve aussi longue, la nutrition est la quatrième discipline. Et elle dépend aussi de ton allure : plus tu pars vite, moins tu digères.

Ces repères valent aussi pour un marathon ou un trail de plus de 2h30.

📌 Enregistre ce post pour ta prochaine prépa.
📩 Tu veux ton plan de course ? Écris-moi « COURSE » en DM.

“Are you looking forward to it?” One question from my coach, and one honest answer: no.

I loved my first 13 months in triathlon, including a full Ironman. But my ego wanted to keep racing, and my body and brain needed a reset.

So no more races until Austria. Right now I’m in prep phase: still training, just with more friends, more strength work and more of my old life back. Soon the big build starts, and I’m so ready for it.

Have you ever signed up for a race for the wrong reasons? 👇

Ironman Kärnten gefinished 

Und neben der Freude über das Finish nehme ich dieses Mal vor allem zwei Erkenntnisse mit, die weit über den Sport hinausgehen.

Die erste: Es ist nie falsch, um Hilfe zu bitten.

Nach dem Radfahren im anspruchsvollen Gelände hatte ich mit starken Krämpfen zu kämpfen. In so einem Moment merkt man schnell, dass Wille allein nicht immer reicht. Ich hatte das Glück, an einer Verpflegungsstation auf eine Physiotherapeutin unter den Volunteers zu treffen, die mir geholfen hat, weiterzumachen. Ohne diese Unterstützung wäre das Finish sehr wahrscheinlich nicht möglich gewesen. Genau darin steckt für mich eine wichtige Botschaft: Wir müssen nicht alles alleine schaffen. Oft ist es gerade die Bereitschaft, Hilfe anzunehmen, die am Ende den Unterschied macht.

Die zweite Erkenntnis: Die besten Teams entstehen manchmal genau dann, wenn man sie braucht.

Im Marathon habe ich zwei Mitstreiter getroffen, mit denen mich sofort ein gemeinsames Ziel verbunden hat: durch eine schwierige Phase zu kommen und das Rennen erfolgreich zu beenden. Jeder von uns hat etwas anderes eingebracht – Verpflegung, Tempo, Orientierung. Ohne große Abstimmung, ohne Hierarchie, einfach aus der Situation heraus. Und genau das hat funktioniert. Für mich ist das ein starkes Bild dafür, wie Zusammenarbeit oft wirklich entsteht: nicht immer geplant, aber wirksam, wenn Vertrauen, gegenseitige Unterstützung und unterschiedliche Stärken zusammenkommen.
